item.title: ‘Pressure Points’ exhibit on Guam highlights printmakers, global collaboration
item.description: What began as a shared conversation among printmakers from different parts of the world has taken shape on Guam through “Pressure Points,” an international exhibition that explores how art can carry the weight of lived experience.

item.title: What does the Jones Act waiver mean for Guam?
item.description: “This waiver opens the door to an untapped domestic fuel market by allowing Guam’s fuel suppliers to access direct shipments of American fuel using foreign vessels,” Sen. Jesse Lujan said.

item.title: New pico-hydro power stations bring Vanuatu closer to green energy goal
item.description: Vanuatu has officially commissioned three pico-hydro power stations on Pentecost Island, advancing toward its goal of making renewable electricity available to remote communities.

item.title: A blooming business: Guam gets a preview of Taiwan
item.description: A burst of color filled the center court of Agana Shopping Center in Hagatna as a two-day orchid exhibition opened its doors on March 27, bringing to Guam a slice of Taiwan’s floriculture, famed for smart cultivation.

item.title: Marshall Islands declared a state of economic emergency amid global criss
item.description: Marshall Islands President Hilda Heine has declared a 90-day state of economic emergency in response to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, which has pushed global fuel costs anticipated to affect local consumer prices.

item.title: Navigating the DISID labyrinth
item.description: In April, as with every April, we will see autism awareness banners, the Marine Corps Drive waves, government proclamations and all the usual lip service about our compassion for people living with disabilities.

item.title: Lack of awareness month: The abandoned end of the spectrum
item.description: While the film successfully introduced autism to a mainstream audience, I would learn years later that it is depicted through a cinematic aperture. It oversimplifies the day-to-day challenges faced by individuals with disabilities and their families.

item.title: Drone testing near Guam highlights expanding US effort to counter emerging aerial threats
item.description: Training teams associated with the counter-drone program have deployed to Guam to work with local military units, including members of Task Force Talon and Guam National Guard security forces.

item.title: Lopsided deal: Legal analysis raises concerns over Tonga
item.description: When Pacific leaders gather to discuss the future of deep-sea mining, the conversation often centers on economic opportunity. For Tonga, that promise has come with a complicated legal trade-off now drawing scrutiny across the region.

item.title: National Geographic expedition studies reef resilience in Marshall Islands
item.description: By Ron Rocky ColomaFor scientists, there are still places in the Pacific where the map feels unfinished.In the Marshall Islands, that sense of discovery is not just about what remains unknown, but what has endured. item.description: Beginning April 12, the company’s carriers serving the region will increase their fuel surcharge again—to 21.5 percent for Guam and the Northern Mariana Islands and 23.5 percent for Micronesia.
